review_notes: Read the whole target file (132 lines) and the related modules BranchCoupling.lean, CompactSeparation.lean, CoulombEstimates.lean, Model.lean, BranchInterfaces.lean and the consumer ExistenceFromLocalGeometry.lean, plus the relevant Mathlib declarations (MeasureTheory/Measure/Typeclasses/Finite.lean, Typeclasses/Probability.lean, Measure/Map.lean, Constructions/BorelSpace/Metric.lean). Verified that E3-specific declarations in this file are used only through topological/set-theoretic facts, and that the finite-cost theorem only needs a finite measure on branchCoupling. All proofs are compiled in the supplied source, but the proposed replacements were not compiled by me; the finite-measure generalisation would need explicit instance derivation using `Measure.isFiniteMeasure_map`, `isFiniteMeasureAdd` and `Measure.smul_finite (by norm_num)`.

findings.excerpt:
theorem finite_cost_branchCoupling
    {nu : Measure E3} [IsProbabilityMeasure nu] {K : Set E3} (hK : IsCompact K)
findings.problem: The theorem asks for a probability measure `nu`, but the proof only uses finiteness of the measure `branchCoupling nu (H 0) (H 1) (H 2) (H 3)` that it integrates against, via `CoulombEstimates.lintegral_coulombCost_lt_top_of_ae_separated`, which requires only `[IsFiniteMeasure mu]`. Nothing in the argument uses `nu Set.univ = 1`: `exists_ae_separated_branchCoupling` does not depend on normalisation, and the finiteness of the coupling (branchCoupling is a `(1/6)`-scaled sum of six maps of `nu`) only needs `nu` finite. So the statement is unnecessarily specialised to probability measures.
findings.proposed_change: Weaken the hypothesis to `{nu : Measure E3} [IsFiniteMeasure nu]`. In the proof, replace `have := isProbabilityMeasure_branchCoupling nu (hH 0) (hH 1) (hH 2) (hH 3)` by an explicit finiteness instance for the coupling, for example `have : IsFiniteMeasure (branchCoupling nu (H 0) (H 1) (H 2) (H 3)) := by unfold branchCoupling; exact Measure.smul_finite _ (by norm_num)`, relying on the instances `Measure.isFiniteMeasure_map` and `isFiniteMeasureAdd` for the six summands. Then apply `CoulombEstimates.lintegral_coulombCost_lt_top_of_ae_separated` with the `eta`/`hae` obtained from `exists_ae_separated_branchCoupling hK hnu hH hcont hdisjoint` exactly as now. Degenerate case: the zero measure is finite and is allowed, and the conclusion `∫⁻ t, coulombCost t ∂... < ⊤` remains true (the coupling is then zero).
findings.benefit: Users with non-normalised base measures (a density measure before renormalisation, a restriction of a probability measure to a subset, a weighted measure) can apply the theorem directly, and the statement then matches the hypothesis of the underlying `lintegral_coulombCost_lt_top_of_ae_separated` instead of adding a stronger assumption that is never used. Existing probability-measure callers are unaffected, since `IsProbabilityMeasure` gives `IsFiniteMeasure`.

findings.problem: These three declarations are fixed to `E3 = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3)`, although none of them uses Euclidean structure: `components` is a plain `Fin.cases` on sets, `compact_components` only invokes `IsCompact.image_of_continuousOn` (line 22), and `disjoint_components_mono` (lines 106–114) only uses `image_mono` and `Disjoint.mono`. The general separation engine they feed, `exists_uniform_compact_separation` in CompactSeparation.lean, is already stated for an arbitrary `[MetricSpace α]` and an arbitrary finite index type, so the E3-specific combinators are the only part of the pipeline that cannot be reused elsewhere.
findings.proposed_change: Parametrise the type: `def components {α : Type*} (K : Set α) (H : Fin 4 → α → α) : Fin 5 → Set α := Fin.cases K (fun i => H i '' K)`, `lemma compact_components {α : Type*} [TopologicalSpace α] {K : Set α} (hK : IsCompact K) {H : Fin 4 → α → α} (hH : ∀ i, ContinuousOn (H i) K) : ∀ i, IsCompact (components K H i)` (proof unchanged), and for `disjoint_components_mono` drop all type constraints: `{α : Type*} {K B : Set α} (hKB : K ⊆ B) {H : Fin 4 → α → α} ...` (proof unchanged). Downstream uses such as `BranchSeparation.disjoint_components_mono d.core_subset` and `components d.compactCore d.branch` still elaborate with `α` inferred from `E3`, and `compact_components` remains usable inside `ae_mem_branchMarginal_components` where the union's measurability is derived from compactness.
findings.benefit: The set-level helpers become usable in any topological (or, for the monotonicity lemma, arbitrary) space, matching the generality of `exists_uniform_compact_separation` and the metric-space statements in CoulombEstimates.lean; the generalisation records that no Euclidean Structure is involved and costs no new mathematics.
